argument_summary: The strongest admissible position is narrower than clean compliance: the record supports proceeding with certification only as a constrained, weakly supported launch decision because aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were observed, and the rollout starts at 4% with rollback and monitoring. The same record also shows the enterprise refund workflow weakness remains exposed, the draft risk acceptance is incomplete and not approved, and rollout controls do not by themselves cure the disclosure issue. The audit concern is therefore overstated if it treats the packet as claiming the weakness was resolved; the supportable claim is that certification proceeds with the limitation carried forward and not treated as remediated.
claims_about_business_cost: There is launch-delay cost if this is escalated, but that cost is not offered as a policy substitute. The narrower point is that the existing evidence already supports a reversible, monitored deployment posture, so further escalation is not necessary merely to reject an overbroad interpretation that the packet claimed full resolution.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts both ways here. It permits rollout controls and monitoring to matter operationally, but it does not let those controls substitute for disclosure, exclusion of the affected use case, or approved risk acceptance when the exposed segment remains in scope. On the admissible record, certification should not be treated as clean compliance. The defensible reading is caveated certification with the unresolved disclosure weakness explicitly preserved in the record, rather than escalation on the theory that the packet falsely claimed full cure.
concessions: The enterprise refund workflow segment remains below target and remains eligible for the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not specifically address enterprise refund workflow exposure.
The policy requires disclosure unless the weakness is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls, a 4% start, rollback capability, and monitoring do not by themselves satisfy that disclosure predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
No new admissible evidence in this record proves that the required disclosure was completed before certification.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel content is relied on as public support.
